metadata.title: Palantir Stock Faces Crucial AI Growth Test

content.text:
This article first appeared on GuruFocus.
Palantir Technologies (NASDAQ:PLTR) heads into second-quarter earnings with expectations set exceptionally high, as Wall Street looks for revenue growth above 80% and evidence that surging defence and artificial-intelligence demand can justify the stock's premium expectations. Analysts forecast adjusted earnings of $0.35 per share on revenue of roughly $1.81 billion.
Palantir develops software that integrates complex data for governments and businesses. Its Gotham platform supports defence and intelligence operations, while Foundry and its Artificial Intelligence Platform help commercial customers deploy AI across operational workflows.
Government demand remains a major catalyst. Palantir's Maven system has become an official Pentagon program of record, strengthening the company's position as the U.S. and its allies increase spending on battlefield intelligence, targeting and command-and-control systems.
Oppenheimer analyst Param Singh expects U.S. government revenue to grow in the low-80% range, supported by increased Department of Homeland Security spending and conflict in the Middle East. Singh also expects Palantir to raise its full-year revenue-growth outlook above 75%, compared with its current 71% forecast.
Commercial execution is the larger uncertainty. U.S. commercial revenue surged 133% year over year to $595 million in the first quarter, while remaining deal value climbed 112% to $4.92 billion. However, Citi expects growth to rebound following a sequential slowdown, while RBC has flagged possible enterprise churn and uncertainty around AIP monetization.
Our checks remain skeptical on the Commercial side, suggesting ongoing churn discussions among enterprise clients, RBC analyst Rishi Jaluria said.
Investor Takeaway On Palantir Stock
Palantir reports after the market closes on Monday, Aug. 3. Investors should focus on U.S. commercial growth, customer retention, deal value and whether management raises its full-year guidance above 75%.
Government strength could support another beat, but the stock's more than 30% year-to-date decline shows that strong headline growth alone may not be enough. A convincing rebound in commercial momentum and sustained operating margins would strengthen the investment case; weaker retention, cautious guidance or limited evidence of AIP monetization could extend the selloff.
